rendered: The separated cathode powder was calcined in air at[1] 600 °C[2] for 2 h[3]. Its purpose, as the Methods state, was to remove the surface coating and the carbon black (CB) left on the powder.[4][5] The TGA-DTG data support this choice: the organic coating layer and the CB both lose mass at temperatures that calcining in air can remove. The paper says both are removed by calcining in air at[6] 600 °C[7]. SEM images after calcination confirmed removal of the coating layer and elimination of CB, and the XRD patterns showed the crystal structure was not damaged.
